title: The shark may be broken- but how is the play? #thesharkisbroken #play...
transcript: So I just got back from the first preview of The Shark Is Broken and these are my thoughts! Now, coming into this play I was under the impression that this was a play ABOUT the making of Jaws and that's not really what this show is. It is more so a play that takes place DURING the making of Jaws. Which is to say that for a lot of it the making of Jaws and the film itself kind of takes a backseat to just these 3 characters hanging out, talking about life, talking about their careers. Now I think that this is both a good thing and a bad thing.  On one hand, I don't think that you need to know a lot about Jaws to enjoy the show. Because jaws is very much happening in the background and this is more so a play about the 3 actors. I also view it as a bit of a negative, because it is very much a show that is just 3 guys sitting in a room talking about stuff and that is not a genre of show that I think is gonna vibe with everyone. And if that is a style of show that you like, I think that you will really enjoy this play!  It is incredibly well done with a really great set and 3 really great performances from the 3 lead actors. For me Alex Brightman is the standout comedically, he is so funny in this, but he has also given some really great dramatic moments. And it's really cool to see this different side of him! Then of course you also have Ian Shaw playing his own father Robert Shaw. Ian also co wrote the script and it's really cool to see his own perspective on his father. It's definitely not entirely positive, and I will say his performance is really great! I initially thought that the casting could be kind of gimmicky, but I thought he really stood on his own and gave a fantastic performance! And then Colin Donnell is the 3rd member of the trio and he has definitely given the least amount to do in the show. But he does have a scene in a Speedo, so if that's something you're into let's just say you will really enjoy his performance 👀 So yeah overall I think it is a really great production of a play that just didn't resonate with me. But I definitely don’t think that means that it won't resonate with you. Especially if you are a Jaws fan, if you are a film/movie fan, especially movies of this decade, I really think that you will enjoy this play! But if you are not, and like me you do not like these slice of life type shows, then this one probably isn't for you.
reasoning: The reviewer acknowledges it's a 'really great production' with strong performances but clearly states the show 'didn't resonate with me' and warns it's not for everyone. They recommend it conditionally for Jaws/film fans while discouraging those who don't like slice-of-life shows.
